elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered 28.1: "This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York." The prior Singapore law and Singapore exclusive jurisdiction wording is removed.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Retained 28.2: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction... Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court..." The carve-out is limited to temporary injunctive relief and so preserves the exclusive merits forum; the conflicting Singapore forum sentence in 28.1 is deleted.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered 28.1 selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. (Immaterial, since the preferred level is fully met.)

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Forum is New York County courts under 28.2, not Delaware/California/London. (Immaterial, since the preferred level is fully met.)

elements.element: [conditional] Temporary injunctive relief carve-out does not defeat exclusivity
elements.evidence: Condition applies and is satisfied: the carve-out in 28.2 is confined to "temporary injunctive relief" to protect confidential information or IP, which the rule treats as customary and non-defeating of an exclusive merits forum.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: 28.1 now designates New York law and retained 28.2 supplies exclusive New York County state and federal court jurisdiction with only a temporary injunctive relief carve-out.

The edit changes only the jurisdiction words and deletes the conflicting Singapore forum clause, consistent with the redline guidance to replace only the jurisdiction words and forum; no survival tails, procedures, or extraneous terms were added.

Intent preserved: 28.2's submission to personal jurisdiction, venue/inconvenient-forum waiver, and injunctive-relief carve-out survive intact; the deletion of Singapore jurisdiction removes rather than creates a contradiction, and leaves no dangling cross-reference or undefined term.

Fallback elements are not met by design (New York rather than Delaware/California/England and Wales), which is acceptable because a single complete level suffices; the margin comment correctly offers the fallback without conceding it in operative text.
Deterministic checks (operation applied, accepted governing law, minimality, element coverage) are consistent with the substantive reading of the rendered text.
